title: Contemporary praise can reward conventional writing
date_or_period: Tang dynasty; letter to Feng Su
writing_problem: How should a writer interpret a conflict between personal quality judgment and immediate audience approval?
context: Han Yu contrasts writing he personally values with conventional writing produced for occasions and describes opposite audience reactions.
constraints: Conventional writing can be immediately legible and rewarded.
A writer may be pursuing standards not optimized for contemporary approval.
alternatives_or_contrasts: Use immediate approval as the main quality signal.
Abandon an unfamiliar writing program because readers find it strange.
decision_action: Do not automatically equate immediate praise with writing quality when the audience may be rewarding conformity; maintain an independent criterion and distinguish long-term writing aims from short-term acceptance.
textual_observation: The letter says writing Han Yu finds satisfying is often judged strange, while conventional occasional writing that embarrasses him is praised.
alternative_interpretations: This is partly a polemical self-positioning statement and may exaggerate the opposition between Han Yu and contemporary taste.
For platform writing, immediate reader response can be a legitimate objective; this heuristic must pass audience-goal fit before activation.
